references.text: The brothers plan to kill Joseph and throw him into a pit, which leads to the event in verse 24.
Reuben suggests throwing Joseph into the pit instead of killing him, so that he can rescue him later – this is the direct background for verse 24.
After throwing Joseph into the pit, the brothers pull him out and sell him to Ishmaelite merchants who take him to Egypt.
Jeremiah is thrown into a cistern/pit without water, only mud – a strong parallel to Joseph's experience of being cast into an empty pit.
The brothers later remember Joseph's cry for help when they threw him into the pit and acknowledge their guilt.
'The pit without water' – a strong verbal parallel to the description in Genesis 37:24, used in a prophecy about salvation and deliverance.
The psalmist's cry for help from deep waters and mud can be seen as a figurative parallel to Joseph's distress in the empty pit.
